analysis.investment_thesis: Fabtech is a small-cap turnkey cleanroom engineering player serving pharma with decent ROE (18.1%) and low debt, but it is a lumpy project-based business with weak cash conversion and trades at 27.6x P/E — outside my comfort zone. Not a steady consumer compounder; I would wait for a much lower valuation or longer execution track record.
key_strengths: Clean balance sheet: borrowings just INR 10 Cr on INR 95 Cr equity (D/E ~0.1)
ROCE 21.2% and ROE 18.1% — healthy capital efficiency
Promoter holding strong at 68.49%, revenue CAGR 11% with FY25 jump to INR 150 Cr
key_risks: Project/EPC business — volatile revenue (FY21: 70, FY24: 97) and thin single-digit margins
Poor cash conversion: OCF only INR 3 Cr on INR 13 Cr PAT in FY25; FCF ~0
P/E 27.6x for a INR 270 Cr cyclical industrial is expensive vs 12-20x range I prefer
red_flags: FY25 investing outflow of INR 26 Cr funded by INR 24 Cr equity raise — dilution/expansion risk
Operating CF consistently lagging reported profits — working capital heavy
analysis.detailed_analysis:
This is a niche cleanroom turnkey contractor for pharma — a decent industry tailwind, but structurally a project-execution business, not the predictable consumer-facing compounder I seek. The financials show the volatility I dislike: revenue swung from INR 89 Cr (2020) to INR 70 Cr (2021) back up to INR 150 Cr (2025), and operating profit bounced between INR 1 Cr and INR 16 Cr. ROE (18.1%) and ROCE (21.2%) look good on paper, but the cash flow tells the real story — FY25 PAT of INR 13 Cr produced only INR 3 Cr of OCF, and 5-year cumulative FCF is roughly flat. That's classic working-capital-heavy EPC economics.

The balance sheet is genuinely conservative (borrowings INR 10 Cr, D/E ~0.1) and promoter holding at 68.49% is reassuring, but the INR 24 Cr equity raise in FY25 and INR 26 Cr investing outflow suggest aggressive, capex-led expansion whose returns are unproven. At 27.6x earnings on a INR 270 Cr market cap with thin, lumpy margins and no dividend visibility, the market is paying growth multiples for an industrial contractor. I'd pass at this price and revisit only if valuation compresses to 12-15x with 2-3 more years of consistent cash generation.
